500.author: ink999107
500.body:
## Summary

Turns the transcript into a live run view and lets a finished run be read back:

- **Permissions** — a run that stops for approval renders a card with the pending request, so the decision is made in the conversation rather than in a side channel.
- **Tool cards** — each tool call shows its input, its result and its status; a result that is not in the run state is read from the tool's own substream the first time the card is opened, keeping progress frames and the final result as separate sections.
- **Run folding** — completed steps fold into a summary row, keeping a long run readable while every step stays one click away.
- **Replay** — a finished turn is reconstructed from the persisted run records (`foldRunRecords`, `replayRun`, `RunReplay`, `placeReplays`), so reopening a session shows the same steps, tool output and permission decisions.
- **Reducer and stream** — permission state, tool traces and replay cursors are folded into the existing run state.

## Stack

Part **2 of 6**. The foundation (#499) is merged, so this branch sits directly on `main` and carries a single commit; the incremental change is the [compare against `main`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/compare/main...ink999107:pr/02-run-stream). The later PRs (#501–#504) build on this branch.

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` — 140 passed

## Summary

Adds the third column: a workspace panel over the session's files.

- **File tree** — the session's file listing, with previews opened as tabs and the tree state kept per session.
- **Previews** — text, Markdown and JSON documents render in the tab (JSON pretty-printed); molecular and crystal structures open in a Mol* viewer loaded as its own chunk, so the main bundle does not carry the renderer. Image previews are not part of this PR.
- **Resize** — the splitter between the conversation and the panel drives `--panel-width`; the column and the panel read the same value, so they cannot disagree, and the width is remembered.
- **Uploads** — files can be dropped on the panel or chosen from the composer; uploads go through the session API and refresh the tree.

## Summary

Adds the settings dialog and the pages behind it.

- **Model** — configured models, default model, provider presets, add/remove and a connection test.
- **Skills** — the project's skill selection, read from and written to the project layer.
- **Network** — the sandbox network mode and its domain allowlist.
- **Runtime** — Runner cards for machines registered over SSH (host key, connect log, write-only credentials) and the Runner resource readings, NPU inventory included; the Project's Runner allowlist is edited here, and it includes the local Runner as a target while the machine cards list only remote ones.
- **Dialog** — four pages under two groups, with Escape and a close button; the composer and the sidebar footer open it. A dialog opened on top of it (a confirmation, for instance) claims Escape first, so one key closes only the topmost dialog.

Each page re-reads when it mounts rather than caching between visits, so a change made in one window is visible in another.

504.author: ink999107
504.body:
## Summary

Resumes the most recent session when the app starts.

- `resumeSession` in `session-order.ts` returns the most recently updated session, or `undefined` when a session is already open, so the decision is testable on its own.
- `resumeOnBoot` carries the decision out against the first listing: it acts once, skips a failed read (which is not an empty workspace), and opens a resumed Session the same way a clicked one does. The bootstrap effect is only its caller.
- The resumed session's Project is adopted before it opens. The listing spans every Project, so without this the app could show one Project's conversation while filing the next 新增会话 or upload under another.
- Sessions are still ordered by recency, and the list that was already current in the sidebar is the one the app resumes.

## Stack

Part **6 of 6**, built on #503. The PR is cumulative on `main`; the incremental change is the [compare against the previous branch](https://github.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/compare/pr/05-language...pr/06-resume).

- `pnpm ci:e2e` — preparation could not download Chromium in this environment, so no E2E case was executed

515.author: zhaozhaozz
515.body:
Daily research workers stopped before model calls when `ubuntu-latest` moved to Ubuntu 26.04 / CPython 3.14.4: NumPy 2.2.6 and SciPy 1.15.3 have no matching wheels, and the fallback SciPy build fails looking for OpenBLAS. Keep the new Ubuntu and Python, and install supported wheels instead.

Closes #514.

## Changes

- Share the seven benchmark dependency pins between real preparation and offline research regression checks. Update only NumPy to 2.3.5 and SciPy to 1.16.3; retain pandas 2.3.3 and the other existing direct versions.
- Default both benchmark entry points to Python 3.14, with a dedicated `SCIENCE_RESEARCH_PYTHON` override. The PR research check previously inherited the gateway's Python 3.12, which could hide this failure. Product service environments keep their existing interpreters and dependencies.
- Require wheels in both entry points so missing wheels fail during resolution instead of starting native builds.
- Add a Biomni preparation regression that resolves the installed Hub API, supplies local download fixtures, verifies the pinned files and rejects corruption.

[NumPy 2.3.5](https://pypi.org/project/numpy/2.3.5/#files), [SciPy 1.16.3](https://pypi.org/project/scipy/1.16.3/#files) and [pandas 2.3.3](https://pypi.org/project/pandas/2.3.3/#files) publish CPython 3.14 Linux AMD64/ARM64 wheels. These pins satisfy the fixed DRB revision's [dependency lower bounds](https://github.com/Ayanami0730/deep_research_bench/blob/852f4022d1f98fb707222e395405136e8f0e8d52/requirements.txt). The Biomni upstream environment files remain verified provenance inputs, not an installed evaluator environment. Benchmark revisions, scoring and real-case evidence assertions are unchanged.

## Validation

Tested tree committed as `916c190b63635581df14ef43aa7938771a8189b3`.

| Check | Environment | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Old numerical pins with wheel-only installation | Clean Ubuntu 26.04.1 container, system CPython 3.14.4, AMD64 | Expected resolution failure: NumPy 2.2.6 has no usable wheel |
| `bash .ci/prepare-real-research.sh` (DRB branch), `uv pip check`, dependency imports | Same target container; no BLAS development packages or compiler installed | PASS: 21 packages installed without source builds, fixed DRB checkout prepared, no broken requirements |
| `bash .ci/run-research-python.sh unit` | Same target container; generic service test interpreter deliberately set to a nonexistent path | PASS: Biomni 19/19, DRB 16/16; zero skips/failures. Includes numerical clustering/association checks and the fixed upstream RACE/FACT pipeline with mocked model/fetch responses |
| Biomni prepare/verify and DRB evaluate CLI imports (`--help`) | Same target container | PASS: 3/3 |
| `pnpm ci:selftest` | Host Ubuntu 24.04 | PASS: 83/83, zero skips/failures |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | Host Ubuntu 24.04 | PASS: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4; zero skips/failures |
| Shell syntax and `git diff --check` | Host | PASS |

## GitHub CI

[PR run 40060251093](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40060251093) completed successfully for PR head `916c190b63635581df14ef43aa7938771a8189b3`, tested as GitHub's PR merge candidate `f823875ea77975e228b4009f2fdc813dddc82379`.

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| UT | 4,754 | 4,754 | 4,754 | 0 / 0 |
| ST | 24 | 24 | 24 | 0 / 0 |
| Mocked browser E2E (combined four workers) | 101 | 101 | 101 | 0 / 0 |

L1, Coverage and `merge-gate` also passed. The uploaded UT evidence confirms `research test Python: 3.14`, with Biomni 19/19 and DRB 16/16 passing. Real/distribution jobs are outside the PR profile and were not run.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the normal PR mocked browser plan: 101/101 journeys passed across the literature, research, standard-config and standard-journeys workers, on the merge candidate above with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research worker accounted for 20/20. This dependency-only change introduces no new product journey; the existing product assertions remain intact.

The actual preparation CLI and offline benchmark pipeline were exercised separately in the target Ubuntu/Python container. No paid model calls, full real-research matrix or gated dataset download were run; ARM64 wheel availability was checked in PyPI metadata, not by executing ARM64. Full product UT/ST/browser E2E layers were not rerun locally; their results above come from GitHub CI.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: restores research benchmark preparation on the new runner image. No product configuration migration is required.
